source.title: Sample Compression, Support Vectors, and Generalization in Deep Learning

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Introduces network support vectors as a proposed generalization measure, derives a sample-compression bound, and reports experiments relating support-vector counts to architecture and label noise. It does not measure the training–test error gap for the claim versions listed.
record.gate_note: The paper reports support-vector fractions and compares max-margin classifiers with trained networks. These are results on proposed proxies or related behavior; the paper does not report the claim versions’ specified test-error sweeps, sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal results.
record.test_reason: The study tests a proposed support-vector description of generalization, rather than any listed version. Its width and depth sweeps measure support-vector fractions, not held-out error. Random-label networks achieve zero training error, but the study does not report the paired natural-label and random-label held-out accuracies needed for V1. Its classifier comparison evaluates the max-margin assumption.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under idealized zero-error and max-margin assumptions, the authors derive a sample-compression generalization bound using network support vectors. They report preliminary architecture and label-noise trends and empirical similarity between trained networks and associated max-margin classifiers; they do not establish that the max-margin assumption holds generally.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a learned path-space embedding and maximum-margin support vectors, rather than directly testing the claim versions’ interventions or train–test error comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Support-vector fraction varies with width, depth, and label randomization; the reported depth trend for the CIFAR convolutional setting is noisier. In the weight-sign experiment, the authors say the finding depends on suitably small initialization and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Support-vector fraction increases approximately logarithmically with width and decreases with depth in the tested MNIST networks; the convolutional CIFAR depth trend is noisier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network support-vector fractions depend on architecture in these binary classification settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label networks fit the training data perfectly and have support-vector fractions approximately 0.5 higher than the natural-label condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random labels require more network support vectors than natural labels in the tested MNIST setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Train and test examples share relatively few distinct path-activation patterns as training-set size varies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned path embeddings exhibit coordinated activation patterns in the tested MNIST networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Network and max-margin validation accuracies are similar, with prediction agreement of 0.990–0.995 across tested depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A max-margin classifier on the learned embedding closely approximates the trained network on binary CIFAR validation data.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory
record.problems: The central max-margin assumption is explicitly idealized and its validity is not established. The architecture sweeps report support-vector counts rather than test error, use limited settings, and average three runs without stated error bars. The paper describes its architecture relationships as preliminary and says additional study is needed. The convolutional generalization theory is not developed in the paper’s stated setting.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Figure-only sweeps are retained as rows with figure-only values because their trends are described in the text.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe, with random-label held-out accuracy at chance.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with measured generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Accuracy after removing examples selected by their memorization influence versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Support vectors here are not memorized examples under V8's inclusion-influence definition. The theoretical risk bound and its depth trend do not substitute for measured held-out error. Agreement is at least 99%, rather than strictly above 99% at every depth.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare training and held-out accuracy for natural versus random labels or report chance-level held-out accuracy.
Varies width and measures support-vector fraction, not test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected test error as described in the version.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out performance.
Does not compare batch sizes or their held-out performance.
Does not test dropout or weight decay effects on held-out error.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.
